Christine’s grandmother’s people came from the northern tip of Alsace, the villages around Wissembourg on the German
border — Stundwiller, Altenstadt, Oberroedern — and from Bavaria.
Between the 1830s and the 1850s that corner of France sent emigrants by the thousand.
Farms shrank with each inheritance, the harvests failed in 1846 to 47 and again in the mid-1850s,
and young men faced the conscription lottery and seven years in the army.
Alsatians went overland to Le Havre, where cotton ships back from America sold cheap passage westward.
Dominick Fritz and Barbara Noullet were in Seneca County, Ohio, by 1835, among the German-speaking Catholics around
Tiffin. The Bavarian Schmitts landed from Bremen in 1853 and settled in the same county.
Frank Staebell left Stundwiller that year too and farmed near Freeport, Illinois.
Margaretha Phillips of his own village also came over in 1853 and spent two years at Buffalo with her sister before
joining him at Freeport, where they married in 1855.
Then the three families converged on Barclay Township in Black Hawk County, Iowa,
where in 1862 seven Catholic families built a small stone church, the beginning of Saint Francis parish.
Frank Fritz married Catharine Schmidt, and their son John married Frank Staebell’s daughter Mary Ann at Saint Francis
in January 1882, in a double wedding with her sister Caroline.
